name: Synthetic data degradation
blurb: Cover for performance collapse caused by training on synthetic data carrying hidden errors.
summary: Cover for performance collapse caused by training on synthetic data carrying hidden errors.

part_3_high_value_red_flags: An exclusion for any loss arising from the use of synthetic data or data generated by algorithms.
A failure to perform exclusion that bars coverage for the model not meeting performance specifications.
A data quality exclusion that excludes errors or omissions in training data.
A sublimit for artificial intelligence model failure that caps loss at a fraction of the policy limit.
An intellectual property exclusion that removes coverage for copyright infringement arising from training data.
A gradual deterioration exclusion that treats performance collapse as expected wear and tear rather than a covered event.
manuscript_wording_and_carve_backs: Delete any exclusion for synthetic data and replace with a definition that limits exclusion to data known to be defective at inception.
Add a definition of performance collapse that includes degradation below a specified accuracy threshold for a continuous period.
Include coverage for loss of use of the AI model even without physical damage to hardware.
Remove any sublimit for artificial intelligence model failure and provide full policy limits.
Add a contractual liability extension to cover assumed liability for model performance in customer agreements.
Negotiate a retroactive date that matches the inception of the synthetic data training program to avoid prior acts exclusion.

part_4_program_structure_and_limits.bi_waiting_period: A waiting period of twelve to twenty four hours is typical for business interruption triggered by a performance collapse, but longer waiting periods of seventy two hours are often imposed for non physical damage.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.business_interruption: Business interruption coverage should be written on an actual loss sustained basis with an extended period of indemnity of at least one hundred and eighty days to capture the full recovery period after remediation.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.property_eb_equipment: Electronic equipment coverage does not respond to non physical performance collapse, so any equipment breakdown endorsement must be amended to include loss of use due to software or data defects.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.per_occurrence_primary_excess_layered_pr: Because the loss is not physical damage, standard property forms do not apply, so the insured must purchase a manuscript first party cyber or technology performance policy with a per occurrence limit typically between five and ten million dollars.

part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.cgl_primary: A standard commercial general liability policy will not respond because performance collapse is not bodily injury or property damage, so the primary layer must be a technology errors and omissions policy.
part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.paper_basis: Claims made because the degradation is a latent defect that may only manifest long after the policy period and the cause is a continuing condition rather than a discrete event.
part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.excess_umbrella_towers: Excess layers follow form over the technology errors and omissions primary and typically provide additional limits in increments of five million dollars up to a total tower of twenty five million dollars, subject to underwriting appetite.

part_1_core_third_party_liability_exposu: A customer sues for breach of contract when the AI model fails to meet agreed accuracy or uptime due to synthetic data errors.
A downstream user alleges negligence because the model made erroneous decisions that caused financial loss.
A copyright holder claims the synthetic data contained unlicensed copyrighted expressions that were reproduced in model outputs after degradation.
A class action alleges the insured misrepresented the reliability of its AI model trained on synthetic data.
A business partner claims lost profits because the performance collapse disrupted their integrated service.
A regulator fines the insured for deploying a faulty AI system that caused consumer harm.

underwriter_wants_to_know: What proportion of the training data is synthetic and how was it generated?
What validation processes exist to detect hidden errors in synthetic data before training?
Has the insured experienced any prior performance degradation linked to synthetic data?
What contractual obligations does the insured have to customers regarding model performance?
Does the synthetic data incorporate any third party copyrighted material without license?
What is the maximum foreseeable loss if the model performance collapses for all customers simultaneously?
